summary: For a kosher shechitah, a bird needs one of its two simanim (the windpipe and the food pipe) cut, and an animal needs both. Cutting most of a siman counts like cutting all of it.

chunks.en: and two simanim in an animal,
chunks.st: and two simanim in an animal,

chunks.st: his slaughter is valid,

chunks.en: And most of one siman

chunks.st: his slaughter is valid.

summary: Shechting two animals at the same time is kosher. Two people may also hold a knife (or two knives) and shecht one animal together.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts two heads at the same time,
chunks.st: With regard to one who slaughters by cutting two animals’ heads simultaneously,

chunks.en: his shechitah is kosher.
chunks.st: his slaughter is valid.

chunks.en: If two people hold the knife and shecht,
chunks.st: If two people are grasping a knife and slaughtering one animal,

chunks.st: even if each is holding a knife and slaughtering one above and one below, with each one slaughtering at a different point in the neck, their

chunks.en: their shechitah is kosher.
chunks.st: slaughter is valid.

summary: The knife must move back and forth; chopping off the head in one blow is pasul unless the knife is very long. A knife that fell and cut by itself is pasul, and stopping in the middle of shechitah for too long makes it pasul.

chunks.en: If he cut off the head in one blow,
chunks.st: If one decapitated the animal in one motion and did not slaughter the animal in the standard manner of drawing the knife back and forth,

chunks.en: it is pasul.
chunks.st: the slaughter is not valid.

chunks.en: If he was shechting and cut off the head in one blow,

chunks.en: if the knife is as long as a whole neck,
chunks.st: if the length of the knife is equivalent to the breadth of the animal’s entire neck,

chunks.en: it is kosher.

summary: If an animal or bird was shechted and no blood came out, it is kosher. The Tanna Kamma says it cannot become tamei because blood did not make it wet; Rabbi Shimon says the shechitah itself makes it able to become tamei.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts an animal, a wild animal, or a bird,
chunks.st: In the case of one who slaughters a domesticated animal, an undomesticated animal, or a bird,

chunks.en: and no blood came out of them,
chunks.st: and blood did not emerge from them during the slaughter, all of these are

chunks.en: they are kosher, and may be eaten with hands that are tamei,
chunks.st: permitted for consumption and do not require the ritual washing of the hands as they may be eaten with ritually impure [mesoavot] hands,

chunks.en: because they were not made ready to become tamei by blood.
chunks.explain: Food can become tamei only after it gets wet with certain liquids, like blood.
chunks.st: because they were not rendered susceptible to ritual impurity through contact with blood,
chunks.stMore: which is one of the seven liquids that render food susceptible to impurity.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: They were made ready by the shechitah.
chunks.st: They were rendered susceptible to ritual impurity by means of the slaughter itself.

summary: When an animal that is about to die is shechted, it must show a sign of life, like kicking or wagging its tail, for the shechitah to be kosher. A healthy animal needs no sign.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts an animal that is about to die,

chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: The slaughter is valid

summary: A Jew who shechts a non-Jew's animal for him: the Tanna Kamma says it is kosher. Rabbi Eliezer worries the non-Jew is thinking of avodah zarah, but Rabbi Yosei says only the shochet's thoughts count.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts for a non-Jew,
chunks.st: In the case of a Jew who slaughters the animal of a gentile for a gentile,

summary: We may not shecht so that the blood flows into seas, rivers or vessels, because that looks like idol worship. But we may let the blood flow into a pool of water, and onto vessels on a ship.

chunks.en: We may not shecht into seas,
chunks.st: One may not slaughter an animal and have its blood flow, neither into seas,

chunks.en: nor into rivers,
chunks.st: nor into rivers,

chunks.en: nor into vessels.
chunks.st: nor into vessels,
chunks.stMore: as in all those cases it appears that he is slaughtering the animal in the manner of idolaters.

chunks.en: But he may shecht into
chunks.st: But one may slaughter an animal and have its blood flow

chunks.en: a round pool of water,
chunks.st: into a round excavation containing water.

chunks.en: and on a ship, onto vessels.
chunks.st: And on a ship, one may slaughter an animal onto vessels
chunks.stMore: as it is clear that his objective is to avoid sullying the ship.

chunks.en: We may not shecht into a small hole in the ground at all,
chunks.st: One may not slaughter an animal and have its blood flow into a small hole in the ground at all,

chunks.en: but he may make a hole inside his house
